filing-20260807-5196.point: NESCOE supports abeyance so ISO-NE and the PTOs can build a section 205 filing through New England's stakeholder process.
filing-20260807-5196.quote: NESCOE supports ISO-NE and the PTOAC’s request for an abeyance to allow for them to develop a Section 205 filing through New England’s stakeholder process.

filing-20260807-5196.point: The Joint Motion schedules a NEPOOL Participants Committee vote on November 12 and a filing on November 16, 2026.
filing-20260807-5196.quote: the NEPOOL Participants Committee would vote on the Section 205 proposal at its November 12, 2026 meeting and that the parties would make their Section 205 filing with the Commission on November 16, 2026.

filing-20260807-5196.point: NESCOE expects the stakeholder process to strengthen the expected section 205 filing.
filing-20260807-5196.quote: ISO-NE and the PTOAC’s expected Section 205 filing would likely be made much stronger if developed through New England’s robust stakeholder process.

filing-20260807-5196.point: NESCOE sets four principles for any new construct: mitigate ratepayer cost, preserve state authority, prioritize reliability, promote transparency.
filing-20260807-5196.quote: any new regulatory construct should seek to mitigate the ratepayer cost impacts of new large load projects, preserve traditional state authority to regulate large and co-located loads, prioritize reliability, and promote transparency.

motion-el26-72-isone-abeyance.point: The movants commit to file by November 16, 2026.
motion-el26-72-isone-abeyance.quote: ISO-NE and the PTOs will submit the FPA Section 205 filing to the Commission on or before November 16, 2026.

motion-el26-72-isone-abeyance.point: They ask for a shortened comment period and expedited ruling because the response is due August 17.
motion-el26-72-isone-abeyance.quote: respectfully request that the Commission shorten the comment period for this motion to five days and grant expedited treatment

motion-el26-72-isone-abeyance.point: They say more time is needed to develop proposals and present them for stakeholder review.
motion-el26-72-isone-abeyance.quote: additional time is needed to develop those proposals and present them for stakeholder review.

motion-el26-72-isone-abeyance.point: The filing will cover all five reform categories: study processes, cost transparency, co-location rules, flexible load service and generation studies.
motion-el26-72-isone-abeyance.quote: efficient study processes, cost transparency, co-location rules, flexible load service, and generation studies

motion-el26-72-isone-abeyance.point: Study reform will include a large load definition with a size and interconnection voltage threshold, and evaluation of alternative transmission technologies.
motion-el26-72-isone-abeyance.quote: This definition will be based on the characteristics of ISO-NE’s transmission system and will include load size and an interconnection voltage threshold.

report-el26-72-isone.point: ISO-NE says New England has been flat or declining in load and has not yet seen significant large load growth.
report-el26-72-isone.quote: New England has not yet encountered significant load growth attributable to the addition of large loads, such as data centers.

report-el26-72-isone.point: ISO-NE's guiding view is that existing competitive markets can meet upcoming resource adequacy needs.
report-el26-72-isone.quote: ISO-NE believes that New England’s markets are sufficiently mature and flexible to meet upcoming challenges.

report-el26-72-isone.point: Pending projects include a lower Pay for Performance rate, capacity auction reforms, uncertainty reserves and demand flexibility.
report-el26-72-isone.quote: the reduction in the Pay for Performance rate; the Capacity Auction Reforms project; improvements to Surplus Interconnection Service; probabilistic forecasting; uncertainty reserves

report-el26-72-isone.point: ISO-NE says two actions will be needed: large loads bring their own generation and are excluded from the load-side capacity requirement.
report-el26-72-isone.quote: requiring new large loads to “bring their own” incremental new generation; and excluding new large loads from the load-side requirements of the capacity market

report-el26-72-isone.point: ISO-NE intends rules similar to SPP's CHILLS, letting large loads take energy until designated resources and upgrades are in place, subject to curtailment.
report-el26-72-isone.quote: ISO-NE intends to pursue rules similar to the Southwest Power Pool’s conditional high impact large load service (“CHILLS”) rules

report-el26-72-isone.point: ISO-NE expects to file the detailed bring-your-own-generation and capacity exclusion rules in 2027.
report-el26-72-isone.quote: ISO-NE anticipates filing the detailed supporting rules implementing this concept in 2027.

filing-20260709-3012.point: The caption wrongly included Vermont Electric Cooperative, and footnote 10 omitted it.
filing-20260709-3012.quote: The caption in the order inadvertently included “Vermont Electric Cooperative, Inc.” and footnote 10 inadvertently omitted “Vermont Electric Cooperative, Inc.”

filing-20260709-3012.point: The notice deletes VEC from the caption and adds it to footnote 10.
filing-20260709-3012.quote: This errata notice hereby corrects the caption, as shown above, by deleting “Vermont Electric Cooperative, Inc.”

filing-20260709-3012.point: FERC keeps authority to review non-public-utility formula rates as part of ISO-NE's Tariff.
filing-20260709-3012.quote: the Commission retains the authority to review each entity’s formula rates as a component of ISO-NE’s Tariff in an order to show cause directed towards ISO-NE

filing-20260622-5134.point: VEC says it does not challenge the need to address large and co-located load service and calls its request procedural.
VEC says it ceased to be a public utility on August 8, 2005 under the Energy Policy Act of 2005.
filing-20260622-5134.quote: it ceased to be a public utility on August 8, 2005 because the changes to the Federal Power Act effective as of that date exempted electric cooperatives that sell less than four (4) million megawatt hours annually.

filing-20260622-5134.point: VEC says it is similarly situated to the non-public-utility owners already listed in footnote 10.
filing-20260622-5134.quote: VEC is a PTO within ISO-NE but it is a PTO that is similarly situated to all of the other of the non-jurisdictional entities listed in footnote 10 of the Order.

filing-20260622-5134.point: VEC points to the CAISO order, which offered to rescind the show cause order for a non-public utility that asks.
filing-20260622-5134.quote: we will rescind the show cause order against them at their request

filing-20260622-5134.point: VEC requests the caption and footnote corrections, or rescission as an alternative.
filing-20260622-5134.quote: removes VEC from the caption of Docket No. EL26-72-000, which intended to identify only ISO-NE and jurisdictional PTOs; and (2) adds VEC in the list of non-jurisdictional PTO entities in footnote 10.
